page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.7 GHz. System memory is sized at 128 GB RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A defining hardware attribute of this configuration is the bundled 11,520 GB local NVMe SSD array, which is tightly integrated to deliver direct, low-latency, and high-capacity scratch and primary data storage. The instance features no discrete hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results show solid single-core computational execution, placing within the top quartile for stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench 6 single-core scoring at 2,084. Multi-threaded processing scores, including a Geekbench multi-core rating of 12,359 and a PassMark CPU mark of 26,168.72, align with expected median performance for 16-vCPU instances. In-memory operations demonstrate 22.64 million operations per second in Redis tests. While L1-L3 cache throughput remains strong, large-block uncached memory read bandwidth falls into lower performance tiers at 36.77 GB/sec, representing a clear operational consideration for memory-streaming workloads.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the L16aos_v4 eliminates external network storage overhead by provisioning substantial local NVMe capacity alongside dedicated AMD EPYC compute. The combination of dense local solid-state capacity, hardware-accelerated vector instructions including AVX-512, and balanced memory makes it well suited for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data indexing clusters, and large data warehousing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage-optimized instance equipped with 16 vCPUs on 8 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running up to 3.7 GHz. The machine delivers 128 GB of system memory paired with a substantial 11,520 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU execution alongside balanced multi-core metrics, achieving 2,084 in Geekbench single-core and 22.64 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Although uncached bulk memory read bandwidth exhibits performance trade-offs under high saturation, the bundled multi-terabyte NVMe storage architecture offers notable efficiency for I/O-intensive services. The instance is designed for transactional databases, large search indexes, caching platforms, and data warehousing workloads requiring fast, localized disk performance.
